summary.note: Beanstalk Diamond proxy (~219 files). Scoring driven by static.json tainted-sinks (65) + 15 High slither hits, source-confirmed for priority clusters. fundsSafu/noNetFlow/noOutFlow/oneOutFlow are INVARIANT guards (Invariable.sol), NOT access guards — permissionless functions carrying them are still open attack surface. Most arbitrary-send-erc20 High flags are call-site-mitigated (facets pass LibTractor._user() as sender); the live attack surface is reentrancy ordering (CEI) in market/claim flows and oracle-driven season minting.

ite.intent: Manipulate the BEAN price oracle in the same block that sunrise() reads it, so deltaB is wrong and Beanstalk mints/burns the wrong supply, profiting the caller via mispriced soil/pods/rewards.
ite.technique: Permissionless call to sunrise()->gm() at SeasonFacet.sol#37/48; gm() calls stepOracle() (deltaB) then stepSun() (Sun.sol#41) which mints Beans (C.bean().mint at Sun.sol#46) and sets soil/pod issuance; an attacker who skews the Well/pump reserves immediately before the season boundary biases deltaB and the freshly-minted supply distribution.
ite.evasion: Beanstalk relies on TWA pump reserves rather than spot price to resist single-block manipulation; gap is whether the TWA window and the once-per-season cadence fully neutralise a multi-block or first-after-gap manipulation — oracle specialist must confirm the pump freshness/window.

ite.intent: Same as sunrise() but with attacker-chosen reward recipient — drive season advancement on manipulated oracle state to mint Beans and set soil/pod issuance in attacker's favour.
ite.technique: gm(account,mode) at SeasonFacet.sol#48 runs stepOracle()->stepSun()->incentivize(); the whole season step (germination, gauge, sun minting) executes off one oracle read of deltaB. Caller controls timing relative to mempool/Well state.
ite.evasion: require(seasonTime()>current) limits to one call per season; reward is the only direct payout. The economic risk is the indirect mint/soil sizing, not the incentive — needs economic_attack + oracle confirmation of TWA robustness.

ite.intent: Re-enter Beanstalk during the SOP token payout to double-claim Flood plenty, draining the protocol's plentyPerSopToken balance for a non-Bean (possibly hook-bearing) well token.
ite.technique: claimPlenty()->_claimPlenty() (ClaimFacet.sol#95): LibTransfer.sendToken(sopToken,...) at L100 transfers the SOP token to the user BEFORE s.accts[account].sop.perWellPlenty[well].plenty is zeroed at L101 and plentyPerSopToken decremented at L104 — a CEI violation. If sopToken or its To.INTERNAL path yields control, the stale non-zero plenty can be re-read.
ite.evasion: nonReentrant on the external claimPlenty()/claimAllPlenty() blocks classic same-facet reentrancy; gaps are (a) read-only/cross-function reentrancy if another facet reads perWellPlenty mid-flow, and (b) reliance on the SOP well token being a plain ERC-20 with no transfer hook. reentrancy specialist to confirm guard scope and token type.

ite.intent: Loop-claim every whitelisted well's plenty; same CEI/reentrancy surface as claimPlenty across all SOP tokens at once.
ite.technique: claimAllPlenty() iterates getWhitelistedWellLpTokens() calling _claimPlenty per token (ClaimFacet.sol#79); each iteration repeats the send-before-zero ordering at ClaimFacet.sol#100-104. Note: unlike claimPlenty(), this lacks the oneOutFlow invariant guard.
ite.evasion: nonReentrant present but no oneOutFlow flow-accounting guard; if a SOP token has a transfer hook, the unbounded token loop is also a DoS/gas vector. reentrancy + dos specialists to confirm.

ite.intent: Re-enter the marketplace during the Bean payout to a filler to refill/cancel the same order twice, extracting Beans escrowed in podOrders beyond what the order funded.
ite.technique: fillPodOrder()->_fillPodOrder() (Order.sol#79): order balance is decremented at L105 then LibTransfer.sendToken(C.bean(),costInBeans,filler,mode) at L107, THEN _transferPlot at L113 and delete at L115-117. The plot transfer and order deletion happen AFTER the outbound token send; with To.INTERNAL or a Bean-side hook the post-send state is reachable.
ite.evasion: oneOutFlow(C.BEAN) invariant bounds net Bean outflow, and order amount is debited before the send (partial CEI). No nonReentrant on this entry (unlike transferPlot). reentrancy specialist must confirm whether oneOutFlow fully blocks a second fill within the same tx.

ite.intent: Pay for a pod listing and re-enter before the listing/plot bookkeeping settles, acquiring pods without full payment.
ite.technique: fillPodListing() at MarketplaceFacet.sol#31 calls LibTransfer.transferToken(C.bean(), user, lister, beanAmount, ...) (which may use safeTransferFrom on Bean) BEFORE _fillListing settles the plot split; transferToken from L1Libraries flagged arbitrary-send-erc20 because 'sender' is a parameter.
ite.evasion: sender is forced to LibTractor._user() by the facet, so the arbitrary-from slither flag is mitigated at the call site; residual risk is ordering of transfer vs _fillListing. Confirm with reentrancy/logic.

ite.intent: If any facet ever calls LibTransfer.transferToken with an attacker-controllable 'sender', an attacker could move tokens out of an arbitrary holder who has approved Beanstalk (arbitrary safeTransferFrom).
ite.technique: transferToken()->safeTransferFrom(sender,recipient,amount) at LibTransfer.sol#42 uses the caller-supplied 'sender' as the from address (slither arbitrary-send-erc20, High). Exploitable only if a public entry passes a user-controlled sender rather than LibTractor._user().
ite.evasion: All audited call sites (MarketplaceFacet.fillPodListing, etc.) pass LibTractor._user() as sender, so the from address is authenticated. Gap: any new/forgotten caller that forwards a raw address param. access_control + token_integration to grep all callers for a non-_user() sender.

ite.intent: Same arbitrary-from class as transferToken — pull tokens from an arbitrary approver into Beanstalk if a caller passes an unauthenticated sender.
ite.technique: receiveToken()->safeTransferFrom(sender,address(this),amount-receivedAmount) at LibTransfer.sol#67 trusts the 'sender' param (slither arbitrary-send-erc20, High).
ite.evasion: Mitigated at call sites that pass LibTractor._user(); the function also supports fee-on-transfer accounting via before/after balance diff. token_integration: verify the balance-diff handles FoT/rebasing and that no caller passes a raw sender.

ite.intent: Re-enter Beanstalk through the Fertilizer ERC-1155 update/payFertilizer callback path to over-claim rinsable Beans (Sprouts).
ite.technique: claimFertilized() (FertilizerFacet.sol#47) calls C.fertilizer().beanstalkUpdate(...) which (Fertilizer._update at Fertilizer.sol#77) calls back into the diamond via IBS(owner()).payFertilizer(); fertilizedPaidIndex is updated at L52 and Beans sent at L53. The cross-contract callback (Beanstalk->Fertilizer->Beanstalk) is the reentrancy seam.
ite.evasion: No nonReentrant on claimFertilized (only oneOutFlow); the Fertilizer side methods are onlyOwner so only the diamond can invoke them, but the payFertilizer re-entry into the diamond mid-update is the gap. reentrancy specialist to trace the diamond<->Fertilizer round trip.

ite.intent: (Privileged) Owner pulls migrated underlying tokens in; risk is mis-accounting of incrementUnderlying vs the actual received amount, not a permissionless drain.
ite.technique: addMigratedUnderlying() (UnripeFacet.sol#284) enforceIsContractOwner() then safeTransferFrom(LibTractor._user(),this,amount) at L289 and LibUnripe.incrementUnderlying(amount) at L294. amount is trusted rather than measured via balance diff — fee-on-transfer underlying would over-credit balanceOfUnderlying.
ite.evasion: LibDiamond.enforceIsContractOwner() + nonReentrant make this privileged; arbitrary-send-erc20 flag is a false positive (from is the owner). token_integration/logic: check incrementUnderlying vs received-amount for non-standard tokens.

ite.intent: Drain protocol SOP-token reserves by re-entering before plenty is zeroed (the actual CEI-violating body behind claimPlenty/claimAllPlenty).
ite.technique: sendToken(sopToken,plenty,user) at ClaimFacet.sol#100 precedes plenty=0 (L101) and plentyPerSopToken-=plenty (L104).
ite.evasion: Reachable only through nonReentrant-guarded externals; cross-function/read-only reentrancy is the residual path. reentrancy specialist.

ite.intent: Acquire pods or refund Beans twice by re-entering between sendToken and _transferPlot/order-delete.
ite.technique: Order.sol#79: decrement order (L105) -> sendToken (L107) -> _transferPlot (L113) -> delete (L115). Outbound send precedes plot settlement.
ite.evasion: oneOutFlow on the external entry; no nonReentrant. reentrancy/logic to confirm whether oneOutFlow blocks a second fill.

ite.intent: Re-enter during the Bean refund to cancel/refund the same order more than once, draining escrowed order Beans.
ite.technique: Order.sol#134: amountBeans=podOrders[id]; sendToken(C.bean(),amountBeans,orderer) at L137 BEFORE delete podOrders[id] at L138 — classic send-before-delete CEI violation.
ite.evasion: External cancelPodOrder has oneOutFlow but no nonReentrant; _createPodOrder also calls _cancelPodOrder internally. reentrancy specialist: prioritise this send-before-delete.

ite.intent: (Cross-contract reentrancy seam) Re-enter the Beanstalk diamond via payFertilizer during a fertilizer update to corrupt fert accounting / over-pay Beans.
ite.technique: beanstalkUpdate()->__update; the sibling _update (Fertilizer.sol#77) calls IBS(owner()).payFertilizer(account,amount) — an external call back into the diamond — before/while balances[].lastBpf is being written.
ite.evasion: onlyOwner restricts the caller to the diamond, but the diamond->Fertilizer->diamond round trip is unguarded by a shared reentrancy lock across contracts. reentrancy specialist to trace the round trip.

ite.intent: (Cross-contract reentrancy seam) Re-enter via the ERC-1155 _safeMint onERC1155Received hook to manipulate fertilizer balances mid-mint.
ite.technique: beanstalkMint() (Fertilizer.sol#47): _update(account,bpf) -> payFertilizer callback, then _safeMint(account,id,amount) at L59 which triggers IERC1155Receiver(to).onERC1155Received (Fertilizer1155.sol#104). lastBpf set at L58 before the mint hook.
ite.evasion: onlyOwner; standard ERC-1155 receiver hook is the gap if the recipient is a contract. reentrancy/token_integration.

ite.intent: Arbitrary external call with attacker-controlled target/value/data executed in the context that calls Pipeline — move ETH/tokens to any address.
ite.technique: _pipeMem() (Pipeline.sol#82): target.call{value:value}(data) at L88 with fully caller-supplied target/value/data (slither arbitrary-send-eth, High). Reached via pipe()/multiPipe()/advancedPipe() externals.
ite.evasion: Pipeline is a stateless pass-through holding no user funds by design; danger is only if invoked via delegatecall/Farm with the diamond's balance. dos/access_control/logic: confirm no delegatecall path exposes Beanstalk's own ETH/approvals.

ite.intent: Sweep the contract's full ETH balance to msg.sender — if reachable with residual diamond ETH, drain it.
ite.technique: refundEth() (LibEth.sol#16): msg.sender.call{value:address(this).balance}("") at L19 sends the entire balance (slither arbitrary-send-eth, High). Called by DepotFacet/FarmFacet/TokenFacet after farm batches.
ite.evasion: Intended to refund leftover msg.value within a single farm() call; gap is whether address(this).balance can include pre-existing protocol ETH (forced send / other deposits) so the refund over-pays. dos/logic to check for forced-ETH inflation.

ite.intent: Withdraw WETH to ETH and forward to msg.sender — drain if balance accounting is loose.
ite.technique: unwrap() (LibWeth.sol#23): after WETH.withdraw, msg.sender.call{value:amount}("") at L26 (arbitrary-send-eth, High).
ite.evasion: amount is the just-unwrapped amount, scoped to the caller's flow. logic to confirm amount cannot exceed the caller's contribution.

ite.intent: Unwrap this junction's entire WETH balance and send all ETH to an arbitrary 'to' — steal WETH parked in the junction.
ite.technique: unwrapAndSendETH(to) (UnwrapAndSendETH.sol#26): to.call{value:address(this).balance}("") at L30 sends the FULL balance to a caller-supplied address (arbitrary-send-eth, High).
ite.evasion: Junction is meant to be used atomically inside a pipe with no resting balance; gap is any WETH left in the junction between calls becomes claimable by anyone. logic/dos/access_control: confirm balance is always 0 outside a pipe call.

ite.intent: (Privileged migration) Mis-seed fertilizer supply or front-run the one-time L2 reseed initializer to corrupt barn accounting before normal operation.
ite.technique: ReseedBarn.init() (line 47) deploys a TransparentUpgradeableProxy for Fertilizer (L58) and calls mintFertilizers (L64), writing fert.fertFirst/fertLast/bpf/activeFertilizer (L66-69). Runs as a diamondCut init step; if callable out of band the fert ledger is attacker-set.
ite.evasion: Intended to run exactly once via the diamond upgrade; gap is the standard uninitialized-proxy/init-front-run class. upgrade_storage to confirm init guard and proxy admin.

ite.intent: (Privileged migration) Establish fertilizer balances during reseed; wrong inputs over/under-mint fertilizer.
ite.technique: mintFertilizers() (line 72): loops fertilizerProxy.beanstalkMint(account,fid,amount,lastBpf) (L88) seeding per-account fertilizer and the fert linked list (L80-82).
ite.evasion: Reached only from ReseedBarn.init(); trust depends entirely on the reseed data. upgrade_storage/logic to sanity-check the seeded totals against invariants.

ite.intent: (Privileged migration) Mint Beans and seed a Well's reserves during reseed; arbitrary-from transfer if OWNER approval is mis-set.
ite.technique: mintAndSync() (ReseedBean.sol#213): IERC20(nonBeanToken).safeTransferFrom(OWNER,address(well),tokenAmount) at L221 (arbitrary-send-erc20, High) plus a Bean mint to sync Well reserves.
ite.evasion: OWNER is a constant migration source, not attacker-controllable; runs once at reseed. logic/oracle: confirm seeded Well reserves match intended initial price (sets the starting oracle state).

agent_hints.reentrancy: Focus on: _cancelPodOrder() (Order.sol#137 send-before-delete), _claimPlenty() (ClaimFacet.sol#100 send-before-zero), _fillPodOrder() (Order.sol#107 send-before-_transferPlot), claimFertilized()/beanstalkUpdate()/beanstalkMint() (diamond<->Fertilizer round trip + onERC1155Received hook). market fill entries lack nonReentrant (only oneOutFlow); verify cross-function & read-only reentrancy and whether the SOP/Well token has transfer hooks.
agent_hints.access_control: Focus on: transferToken()/receiveToken() (LibTransfer arbitrary-from — grep ALL callers for any sender != LibTractor._user()), Reseed init()/mintAndSync()/mintFertilizers() (one-shot diamondCut initializers — check init guard / proxy-admin / front-run), unwrapAndSendETH() (no caller restriction on full-balance send).
agent_hints.arithmetic: Focus on: addMigratedUnderlying() (incrementUnderlying trusts 'amount' not balance-diff -> FoT over-credit), Sun.setSoilAbovePeg() (mul/div soil sizing), Fertilizer.__update() (deltaBpf*amount). check LibRedundantMath casts (toUint128 in setSoil) and decimal scaling.
agent_hints.oracle: Focus on: sunrise()/gm() -> stepOracle() deltaB (Sun.stepSun mints Beans off this read). Verify the Well/pump TWA window resists single-block & first-after-gap manipulation; mintAndSync() seeds the initial Well reserves (starting oracle state).
agent_hints.flash_loan: Focus on: sunrise()/gm() (flash-skew Well reserves before the season boundary to bias deltaB and minted supply/soil), fillPodOrder()/fillPodListing() (flash Beans to fill+re-enter). Pair with oracle TWA assessment.
agent_hints.logic: Focus on: _fillPodOrder() ordering (sendToken before _transferPlot/delete), _cancelPodOrder() send-before-delete, refundEth()/unwrapAndSendETH() (full address(this).balance sends — forced-ETH inflation / leftover-balance theft), claimFertilized() fertilizedPaidIndex accounting.
agent_hints.dos: Focus on: claimAllPlenty() (unbounded loop over whitelisted well tokens + external sends per iteration), mintFertilizers() (reseed loop), refundEth()/unwrapAndSendETH() (full-balance call can be griefed by a reverting recipient).
agent_hints.economic_attack: Focus on: sunrise()/gm() (permissionless season step controls Bean mint, soil/pod issuance, and caller reward — MEV/timing around oracle), market fills (sandwich pod orders/listings), Fertilizer rinse vs Sun minting interplay.
